public_source_audit.paper: Godin C, Thivierge J-P (2026), Manifold-constrained plasticity enables stable learning in recurrent neural circuits, PLOS Computational Biology, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014719, published 2026-08-25
observed_source_facts: SPLiT combines online Oja subspace tracking with normalized LMS in manifold coordinates.
The estimated basis is re-orthonormalized every 1 ms.
Learning feedback shapes recurrent states during training; the paper explicitly distinguishes constrained and unconstrained feedback paths.
S11 compares frozen versus adaptive estimated decoder subspace and reports higher error when frozen; S12 tests rotational perturbations from 25 to 80 degrees.

The Discussion explicitly acknowledges that low-rank projections or pseudoinverse regularization could provide similar conditioning benefits; the claimed novelty is the biologically motivated online tracking mechanism.

The article declares S1 Code as Code.zip at DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014719.s002. The current tool transport could see the declaration but could not retrieve the binary archive, so no file-level exact reproduction was claimed.

fixed_manifold_equivalence.claim: For a fixed orthonormal manifold x=A z, ambient full-space normalized LMS initialized with w=A v is algebraically equivalent to intrinsic normalized LMS on z: the ambient update remains in span(A) and A^T w follows exactly the same update. Therefore low-rank covariance by itself does not create an optimization disadvantage for per-sample normalized LMS; explicit subspace tracking can only add predictive value when the supported subspace moves, when feedback/regularization changes the dynamics, or when locality/parameter constraints matter.
fixed_manifold_equivalence.scope: This is a mathematical control for fixed orthonormal manifolds and normalized LMS, not a reproduction of the full SPLiT feedback system.

setup.development_tuning: Oja step size, EW-PCA decay, and full-space RLS forgetting were selected on disjoint development seeds before held-out evaluation.
setup.coordinate_budget: oracle, Oja, EW-PCA and frozen trackers each used the same 3-dimensional decoder budget; full-space NLMS/RLS used 64 weights and are reported separately as conditioning baselines.
setup.trajectory: low-rank recurrent-like latent dynamics projected through a gradually rotating orthonormal ambient basis; no source-exact teacher-feedback coupling in this control

interpretation: Adaptive low-dimensional tracking is strongly supported in this reduced rotating-subspace regime: frozen coordinates fail as the manifold rotates.

Oja and generic aligned EW-PCA are essentially indistinguishable at the final endpoint after disjoint tuning; this supports adaptive subspace tracking but does not isolate Oja as the uniquely effective tracker.

Full-space normalized LMS remains stable despite low rank and materially outperforms the frozen low-dimensional decoder, consistent with the fixed-manifold equivalence argument. It is worse than adaptive 3-D tracking during continuous rotation because it accumulates stale directions rather than explicitly compressing to the instantaneous subspace.

A tuned full-space RLS baseline approaches the oracle endpoint, showing that full-space inversion methods are highly sensitive to forgetting/regularization choices; a single poorly tuned FORCE/RLS comparison cannot by itself identify the benefit of Oja tracking.

closed_loop_feedback_analogue.setup: 32 ambient / 3 latent units, leaky recurrent latent dynamics, scalar output error fed back into the latent recurrent state, 12 s trajectories, 80-degree gradual subspace rotation, 20 held-out seeds. This preserves the qualitative feedback coupling but not the source code, default table or exact Eq.14 implementation.
scope: The Oja result is parameterization-specific and cannot be treated as evidence against the paper because the exact source learning-rate scaling, centering, feedback transform and default parameters were unavailable without Code.zip.

The important result is prioritization: generic adaptive subspace tracking and ambient normalized LMS both remained competitive under feedback, so exact-source comparisons to these controls are more diagnostic than another synthetic Oja-only run.

candidate_update.new_interpretation: The strongest transferable mechanism is adaptive low-dimensional subspace conditioning under representational drift. Oja provides a local Hebbian implementation, but current evidence does not isolate Oja from generic online PCA/subspace tracking. A fixed-manifold algebraic control shows that low rank alone does not disadvantage full-space normalized LMS, and reduced rotating-subspace tests show tuned full-space RLS/NLMS can remain competitive. Exact source-code tests are therefore required to separate online tracking, feedback shaping, low-dimensional conditioning and Oja locality.
scope: Do not generalize the reduced controls to the published recurrent tasks or claim a failure of SPLiT.

The PLOS source explicitly acknowledges that low-rank projections/pseudoinverse regularization could yield similar conditioning; these controls refine that caveat rather than contradict the paper wholesale.
Biological locality and computational predictive performance are distinct dimensions: EW-PCA is a useful computational control but not a local synaptic rule.

exact_next_action: Recover PLOS S1 Code (DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014719.s002) through a file-capable public transport and reproduce S11/S12 or the constrained 2-Hz sine condition with the exact default parameter table and Eq.14 feedback. In that source-exact implementation add: (1) full-space normalized LMS, because it is algebraically equivalent to intrinsic NLMS on a fixed orthonormal manifold; (2) aligned EW-PCA or another generic online subspace tracker + the same NLMS with the same latent coordinate budget; (3) tuned full-space RLS/ridge/pseudoinverse controls; and (4) frozen estimated manifold. Use identical seeds and measure MSE, convergence time, principal angle, decoder-update norm, noise sensitivity, rotational-drift recovery and autonomous replay. If Code.zip remains inaccessible, obtain the article JATS/XML/default table through another public text transport before further synthetic experiments.
